confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living figures found in web searches. These were crowd-sourced Numbeo-style averages reported by Expatica for June 2026, plus MyLifeElsewhere and travel-guide price ranges. Prices were converted at about 1.10 USD per EUR, a figure implied by a third-party republication of RBA cross rates around November 2026. I raised the mid-range meal a little above the roughly EUR 52 average to allow for the July peak season. The sources disagree on the mid-range meal (EUR 25-40 vs about EUR 52) and on the inexpensive meal (pintxos at EUR 8-14 vs sit-down meals averaging about EUR 19). Wine is based on guide ranges of about EUR 2.50-3 per glass at pintxo bars, raised slightly for a restaurant pour. I found no reliable current cocktail prices. The only data point was a 2013 report of EUR 9 premium gin-tonics, so the cocktail anchor is based on the local ratio of cocktails to beer and is uncertain. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, with no booking pages or listings checked. They reflect San Sebastian's very high July peak-season rates, limited hotel supply and premium resort pricing, so they are the least certain anchors. FX provenance: the search summary reported RBA AUD/USD 0.6720 for 2026-11-18, but this came via a search result and a third-party republication. I did not open the official rba.gov.au page, and the source_url points to the RBA exchange-rate page for verification.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink are based on San Sebastian-specific aggregated data, which puts it about 15-20% above the Spanish average. Accommodation is benchmarked against peak-summer pricing in high-demand northern Spanish and southwest French coastal resort cities such as Biarritz, and against central Barcelona and Madrid. San Sebastian's July hotel rates are typically at or above those cities' rates.
